cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Receive a PM invitation sent by the Super Administrator
cases.pre: Super Administrator facilitator is signed in to Accounts. PM-SA uses a new, accessible test email address.
cases.steps:
1. Super Administrator: open the account invitation form.
2. Enter the test user's first name, last name, email and Project Manager role; submit.
3. PM tester: open that inbox and find the invitation.
4. Open its link in a separate browser session.
cases.expected: An invitation is received at the entered address and opens account setup for the invited user. The assigned role is Project Manager. Record delivery problems as a failure or environment blocker; do not claim a successful invitation from the on-screen message alone.

cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Receive a PM invitation sent by the Administrator
cases.pre: Administrator facilitator is signed in to Accounts. PM-ADMIN uses a new, accessible test email address.
cases.steps:
1. Administrator: open the account invitation form.
2. Enter the test user's first name, last name, email and Project Manager role; submit.
3. PM tester: open that inbox and find the invitation.
4. Open its link in a separate browser session.
cases.expected: An invitation is received at the entered address and opens account setup for the invited user. The assigned role is Project Manager. Record delivery problems as a failure or environment blocker; do not claim a successful invitation from the on-screen message alone.

cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Pending invitation does not give normal portal access
cases.pre: Facilitator provides a pending invitation session that has not completed password setup.
cases.steps:
1. In that session, try opening the PM portal.
2. Observe the screen without completing setup.
cases.expected: Normal protected portal use is blocked until account setup is completed.

cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Reject a setup password shorter than eight characters
cases.pre: PM has opened a valid invitation and remains on account setup.
cases.steps:
1. Enter a seven-character test password in both fields.
2. Select Complete account setup.
cases.expected: Setup does not complete; password-length validation is shown.

cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Reject mismatched setup passwords
cases.pre: PM is on account setup with a valid invitation session.
cases.steps:
1. Enter an eight-or-more-character test password.
2. Enter a different confirmation.
3. Select Complete account setup.
cases.expected: Setup does not complete; confirmation mismatch is reported.

cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Complete invitation activation with the assigned PM role
cases.pre: PM remains on the valid invitation setup page. Use a private test password, not written in this workbook.
cases.steps:
1. Enter matching passwords of at least eight characters.
2. Select Complete account setup.
3. Inspect the destination and account role.
4. Repeat for the other invitation-source test account.
cases.expected: Setup completes and opens the PM portal. No role-selection control permits privilege changes. Both invitation sources can be activated.

cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Sign in using the activated PM account
cases.pre: Activated PM account exists; user has signed out.
cases.steps:
1. Open the login page.
2. Enter the PM email and correct password; submit.
3. Inspect the destination.
cases.expected: PM is authenticated and reaches the Project Manager portal.

cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Reject an incorrect login password
cases.pre: Activated PM account exists; user is signed out.
cases.steps:
1. Enter the PM email with an incorrect password.
2. Submit the login form.
cases.expected: An authentication error appears and protected access is not granted. Exact error wording is not the pass criterion.

cases.section: 01. Invitation and account activation — administrator-assisted setup
cases.title: Verify account details in Settings
cases.pre: PM is signed in; invitation identity is recorded in Test Setup.
cases.steps:
1. Open Settings from the account menu.
2. Compare name, email and role with the invitation.
cases.expected: The account details identify the invited PM correctly.

cases.title: Open the project assigned by an administrator
cases.pre: Admin facilitator has created UAT Project A with the activated PM and an eligible Foreman. Project B is assigned to another PM.
cases.steps:
1. PM: refresh Projects.
2. Open Project A.
3. Inspect project name, PM and Foreman.
cases.expected: Project A is accessible with the configured management assignments. The admin creation is setup, not an action performed by the PM.

cases.title: Deny access to an unassigned project
cases.pre: PM is assigned only to Project A; facilitator supplies the normal URL of disposable Project B.
cases.steps:
1. Inspect Projects for Project B.
2. Open Project B URL in the PM session.
cases.expected: Project B records are not disclosed. A denied/not-found response or safe redirect is acceptable; no particular HTTP code is required for this UAT case.

cases.title: Account management is unavailable to PM
cases.pre: PM is signed in.
cases.steps:
1. Inspect navigation for Accounts.
2. Attempt normal navigation to /admin/accounts.
3. Check for invitation and role-management controls.
cases.expected: PM cannot open account management or invite/manage accounts. This checks the PM boundary, not successful admin account operations.

cases.title: Open the permitted PM modules
cases.pre: PM is signed in.
cases.steps:
1. Open Dashboard, Projects, Team, Inventory and Reports from navigation.
2. Open Settings from the account menu.
3. Return to Projects.
cases.expected: Each permitted screen opens in the PM portal. Settings need not be a sidebar item.

cases.title: Project creation, project-detail editing and deletion remain admin-only
cases.pre: PM is signed in; assigned UAT Project A is open. Use only the disposable UAT records in Test Setup.
cases.steps:
1. Inspect Projects for a creation control.
2. Inspect Project A details for project edit and delete actions.
cases.expected: PM is not offered administrative project creation, detail editing or deletion. Estimate/schedule editing is a separate permitted workflow.

cases.title: Review project dates and distinguish allocated budget from plan
cases.pre: Admin configured A with a PHP 100,000 allocated budget and recorded dates; facilitator has supplied these expected values.
cases.steps:
1. Open A and inspect project information.
2. Compare displayed dates and allocated budget with setup.
3. After planning, compare its planned estimate with the allocated budget.
cases.expected: Displayed project information matches setup. Allocated budget is distinct from the computed planned estimate; they need not be equal.

cases.title: View an assigned completed project
cases.pre: Facilitator supplies an accessible completed UAT project with retained records.
cases.steps:
1. Open the completed project.
2. View its retained progress and report information.
cases.expected: Completed project records remain viewable while stored. This test does not require an immutable archive or universal read-only lock.

cases.title: Browse the four Team categories
cases.pre: PM is signed in; facilitator prepared members in all four categories.
cases.steps:
1. Open Team.
2. Select Management, Skilled Workers, Engineers & Architects, and Subcontractors in turn.
cases.expected: Each tab displays members in its corresponding category.

cases.title: PM cannot change the member master list
cases.pre: PM is viewing Team.
cases.steps:
1. Open a skilled worker record.
2. Inspect available actions for member creation, editing or deletion.
cases.expected: Master-member changes are unavailable to PM. Work-group editing remains a separate permitted feature.

cases.title: Read worker schedule, rate and subcontractor company
cases.pre: Admin prepared UAT Worker W1 at PHP 100/hour, Mon–Sat 8 hours and Sunday 0; subcontractor SC1 has a company name.
cases.steps:
1. Open W1 and inspect rate, daily hours, weekly total and assignments.
2. Open SC1 and inspect its company.
cases.expected: W1 shows the prepared rate, seven-day schedule and 48 weekly hours. SC1 displays its recorded company. This checks display, not admin input validation.

cases.title: Search Team and recover the full list
cases.pre: Team contains W1 and other members.
cases.steps:
1. Search for W1 by name.
2. Clear search.
3. Apply an available role or availability filter and then clear it.
cases.expected: Matching members are returned; clearing controls restores the applicable list.

cases.title: Create a work group
cases.pre: PM is on Team; UAT Crew Alpha does not exist.
cases.steps:
1. Open group creation.
2. Enter UAT Crew Alpha, a short description and select W1 plus a second member.
3. Save and reopen the group.
cases.expected: The group is saved with the entered description and selected members.

cases.title: Reject a case-insensitive duplicate group name
cases.pre: UAT Crew Alpha exists.
cases.steps:
1. Start another group.
2. Enter uat crew alpha and save.
cases.expected: Duplicate name is rejected; no second group is created.

cases.title: Edit group membership without deleting people
cases.pre: UAT Crew Alpha exists; W1 also belongs to UAT Crew Beta prepared by facilitator.
cases.steps:
1. Edit Alpha description and membership, keeping W1.
2. Save and inspect Alpha and W1.
cases.expected: Changes persist; W1 can belong to both groups and remains a Team member.

cases.title: Delete a disposable group
cases.pre: PM created UAT Crew Delete with two members.
cases.steps:
1. Delete UAT Crew Delete using its group action.
2. Check Team for its former members.
cases.expected: Only the group is removed; the member records remain.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Create a project phase
cases.pre: PM is signed in; assigned UAT Project A is open. Use only the disposable UAT records in Test Setup.
cases.steps:
1. Open the project cost estimate/planning controls.
2. Create phase UAT Foundation.
3. Save and reload the view.
cases.expected: The phase appears in Project A and persists after reload.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Rename a phase
cases.pre: UAT Foundation exists in A.
cases.steps:
1. Edit the phase name to UAT Foundation Revised.
2. Save and reload.
cases.expected: The new name persists without adding another phase.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Create a task within a phase
cases.pre: UAT Foundation Revised exists.
cases.steps:
1. Add task UAT Concrete Work to that phase.
2. Enter estimated quantity 100 and unit cu.m using the task form.
3. Save and reopen it.
cases.expected: Task belongs to the selected phase with the entered quantity and unit.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Create and edit a supported subtask
cases.pre: A disposable parent task exists; subtask controls are available.
cases.steps:
1. Use the task subtask control to add UAT Subtask.
2. Enter its supported quantity and cost fields.
3. Save, reopen and change its name.
cases.expected: Subtask is saved under the intended parent and its edit persists. Compare totals with the displayed breakdown; do not count the parent again as a separate leaf.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Plan a standalone phase
cases.pre: A has phase UAT Standalone with no tasks.
cases.steps:
1. Enter its planned quantity, dates and cost components.
2. Open its progress view.
cases.expected: The standalone phase has its own plan and progress entry without requiring a child task.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Maintain task planning fields
cases.pre: Disposable task and valid predecessor task exist.
cases.steps:
1. Edit name, quantity, unit, start/end dates and priority through the applicable controls.
2. Set the supported milestone and predecessor fields.
3. Save and reopen each relevant control.
cases.expected: Entered settings persist. Fields not present in one editing form are maintained through their own controls; saving unrelated fields does not erase them.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Calculate planned cost from four components
cases.pre: Use a clean disposable task; no inherited category extras or amount overrides.
cases.steps:
1. Set planned material PHP 10,000, labor PHP 8,000, equipment PHP 5,000 and other PHP 2,000 using their respective controls.
2. Save and inspect the cost breakdown.
cases.expected: The four components total PHP 25,000 and the displayed project/category totals include the task once.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Maintain planned materials
cases.pre: A clean task is available.
cases.steps:
1. Add Cement with planned quantity 20 bags and unit cost PHP 250.
2. Save and reopen the material breakdown.
cases.expected: The recorded material allowance is 20 bags and PHP 5,000; the task material total reflects it.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Maintain planned equipment cost items
cases.pre: A disposable task has no existing items in this cost component.
cases.steps:
1. Open its equipment cost breakdown.
2. Add two named items for PHP 1,000 and PHP 500.
3. Save and reopen.
cases.expected: Both descriptions and amounts persist; the equipment component totals PHP 1,500.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Maintain planned other cost items
cases.pre: A disposable task has no existing items in this cost component.
cases.steps:
1. Open its other cost breakdown.
2. Add two named items for PHP 1,000 and PHP 500.
3. Save and reopen.
cases.expected: Both descriptions and amounts persist; the other component totals PHP 1,500.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Set a valid default labor percentage
cases.pre: PM is signed in; assigned UAT Project A is open. Use only the disposable UAT records in Test Setup.
cases.steps:
1. Set the project default labor percentage to 20 through its control.
2. Save and reopen the control.
3. Use the supported apply adjustment and inspect the resulting breakdown.
cases.expected: 20% persists and the displayed labor calculation follows the selected adjustment. Compare against the shown calculation basis rather than assuming it is a percentage of total project budget.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Reject default labor percentage -1
cases.pre: PM is signed in; assigned UAT Project A is open. Use only the disposable UAT records in Test Setup.
cases.steps:

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Reject default labor percentage 101

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Verify an explicit amount override
cases.pre: Facilitator supplies a disposable work item whose planning control supports an amount override; records its starting components.
cases.steps:
1. Set an allowed override amount.
2. Save and inspect the component/total explanation.
3. Reopen the item.
cases.expected: The saved amount and resulting total agree with the visible override breakdown. No duplicate amount is added to project totals.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Verify cost-based weight and its explanation
cases.pre: Isolated project fixture: two leaf tasks cost PHP 10,000 and PHP 90,000; no direct phase extras or manual weight overrides.
cases.steps:
1. Open the PHP 10,000 task weight breakdown.
2. Compare task planned cost and project planned cost.
cases.expected: Task weight is 10% of the PHP 100,000 baseline; the breakdown explains the basis.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Assign workers to a task
cases.pre: A contains task T1; W1 and another worker are available in the assignment picker.
cases.steps:
1. Open T1 worker assignment.
2. Select the workers or their group and save.
3. Reopen assignment and W1 profile.
cases.expected: Selected assignment persists and member assignment information identifies the project/task.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Assign workers to a standalone phase
cases.pre: UAT Standalone has no child task; an eligible worker exists.
cases.steps:
1. Open phase assignment.
2. Select the worker and save.
3. Reopen the phase assignment.
cases.expected: The worker is assigned to the standalone phase.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: View the dated Gantt schedule
cases.pre: A contains dated tasks and a milestone.
cases.steps:
1. Open the Gantt schedule.
2. Compare task start/end dates with the timeline.
3. Locate the current-date indicator.
cases.expected: Bars represent the planned dates and displayed progress; current date is identified.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Change schedule dates and undo the change
cases.pre: Disposable dated task; record original dates.
cases.steps:
1. Use a supported schedule control to change dates.
2. Use Undo.
3. Inspect the task dates.
cases.expected: Undo restores the previous supported schedule change.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Redo a schedule change
cases.pre: The preceding schedule change was undone.
cases.steps:
1. Use Redo.
2. Reload the schedule after the operation completes.
cases.expected: Redo reapplies the change and the persisted dates match.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: Account for project working days and holidays
cases.pre: Facilitator prepared the isolated calculation fixture in Test Setup; its dates and automatic days are recorded. Do not use production data.
cases.steps:
1. Facilitator supplies an isolated schedule with Mon–Fri working days and one holiday inside its dates.
2. Inspect expected progress on the agreed test date.
3. Compare with elapsed eligible working days divided by total eligible working days.
cases.expected: Nonworking weekdays and the holiday are excluded from that working-day progress calculation. Do not assume adding a holiday automatically reschedules every task.

cases.section: 04. Cost estimate, work assignment and schedule
cases.title: View admin-created holidays and meetings
cases.pre: Admin has created a holiday and a named meeting with valid start/end times in A.
cases.steps:
1. PM: open the project Calendar view.
2. Inspect the prepared holiday and meeting.
3. Check available event actions.
cases.expected: Recorded holiday and meeting information is visible; administrative event creation/editing is unavailable to PM. This does not test meeting-time validation by an admin.

cases.section: 05. Optional BOM import — use a disposable estimate
cases.title: Extract a reviewable BOM draft from PDF
cases.pre: Facilitator supplies a small valid PDF BOM containing a named task and known material quantities; extraction service is configured. Use a disposable estimate.

cases.title: Correct and apply a BOM draft

cases.section: 05. Optional BOM import — use a disposable estimate
cases.title: Reject an unsupported BOM file
cases.pre: Facilitator supplies a harmless .txt file outside the supported file types.

cases.expected: The line retains all entered details and PHP 10,000 is recorded as material expense. Enter Amount explicitly; it is not assumed to be enforced as quantity times price.

cases.section: 06. Purchases and stock — before daily material usage
cases.title: Record multiple purchase lines in one batch
cases.pre: Use a separate disposable purchase date and material names.
cases.steps:
1. Add one line for UAT Sand and one for UAT Gravel with valid supplier, units, quantities, unit prices and amounts.
2. Save the batch.

cases.expected: Both lines are saved under the selected date with their individual values.

cases.pre: Open a disposable purchase draft with all other required values valid.
cases.steps:

2. Attempt to save.
3. Reopen the purchase list.
cases.expected: The invalid purchase is not saved; feedback identifies the invalid or missing input.

2. Attempt to save.

cases.expected: The invalid purchase is not saved; feedback identifies the invalid or missing input.

cases.title: Reject purchase with negative amount

cases.steps:

cases.expected: The invalid purchase is not saved; feedback identifies the invalid or missing input.

cases.section: 06. Purchases and stock — before daily material usage
cases.title: Reject purchase with missing date
cases.pre: Open a disposable purchase draft with all other required values valid.
cases.steps:
1. In that draft, clear purchase date.
2. Attempt to save.
3. Reopen the purchase list.
cases.expected: The invalid purchase is not saved; feedback identifies the invalid or missing input.

cases.section: 06. Purchases and stock — before daily material usage
cases.title: Attach and open a purchase receipt
cases.pre: Facilitator provides a supported small receipt PDF or image.
cases.steps:
1. Attach the receipt to a valid disposable purchase.
2. Save and open the purchase receipt link.
cases.expected: The supplied receipt can be opened. A saved purchase without the intended receipt is not a pass for this attachment case.

cases.section: 06. Purchases and stock — before daily material usage
cases.title: Update the received quantity
cases.pre: Disposable purchase of 50 pieces exists and currently shows 50 received; no usage exists for that material.
cases.steps:
1. Change received quantity to 30.
2. Save and inspect its stock record.
cases.expected: Received quantity is 30 of 50 and stock is 30. The change is a reduction of 20 from the original 50, not an increase of 30.

cases.section: 06. Purchases and stock — before daily material usage
cases.title: Reject received quantity above purchased quantity
cases.pre: The same 50-piece disposable purchase exists.
cases.steps:
1. Attempt to set received quantity to 51.
2. Save and recheck the purchase.
cases.expected: Value is rejected; saved received quantity is unchanged.

cases.section: 06. Purchases and stock — before daily material usage
cases.title: Detect a stale received-quantity update
cases.pre: Two PM browser sessions show the same disposable purchase with 30 received.
cases.steps:
1. Session A changes received quantity to 35 and saves.
2. Without refreshing, session B attempts to save 40.
3. Reopen the record.
cases.expected: The stale write is rejected; session A value of 35 remains until a refreshed valid update is made.

cases.section: 06. Purchases and stock — before daily material usage
cases.title: Normalize stock grouping by name and unit
cases.pre: Facilitator has prepared two purchases of the same test material with case/spacing variations, matching units, and a known combined received amount.
cases.steps:
1. Open the stock view.
2. Compare the combined balance with received quantities and saved usage.
cases.expected: Equivalent normalized material name/unit records are grouped; different units are not silently combined.

cases.section: 06. Purchases and stock — before daily material usage
cases.title: Display Available stock
cases.pre: Facilitator prepared a separate material with 50 received and 0 saved usage.
cases.steps:

cases.expected: Balance is 50; status identifies available. No particular badge color is required.

cases.title: Display Low stock stock

2. Enter UAT Manual Item, specification, quantity 5, unit pcs and availability status.
3. Save and reopen.
cases.expected: The manual record retains those fields. It does not automatically establish a purchase or a purchase expense.

cases.title: Submit a material request
cases.pre: PM is signed in; assigned UAT Project A is open. Use only the disposable UAT records in Test Setup.
cases.steps:
1. Open the material request form.
2. Add UAT Cement, specification UAT, quantity 50, unit bags, purpose UAT work.
3. Set a required date, select Urgent and enter UAT delivery remarks.
4. Submit and reopen.
cases.expected: The request is Submitted with saved details and a project-specific MR-001-style number. Existing sequences may produce a higher number.

cases.title: Edit a submitted material request
cases.pre: A disposable submitted material request has no fulfillment.
cases.steps:
1. Edit its remarks and requested quantity.
2. Save and reopen.
cases.expected: The eligible edit persists on that request.

cases.title: PM cannot approve a material request
cases.pre: Submitted material request exists.
cases.steps:
1. Open it as PM.
2. Inspect available actions.
cases.expected: Approval is unavailable to PM. Use an Admin/Superadmin facilitator for the following approval setup.

cases.title: Record partial material delivery
cases.pre: Admin approved a separate material request for 20 units; fulfilled quantity is 0.
cases.steps:
1. Open the approved request and its delivery control.
2. Record delivery of 8 units and save.
3. Inspect details.
cases.expected: Fulfilled quantity becomes 8 of 20 and status is Partially fulfilled.

cases.title: Reject excessive material delivery
cases.pre: material request needs 20 units and already has 8 fulfilled.
cases.steps:
